title: A/B power CI scheduling and oncall choreography scratchpad
body:
Goal: lightweight working notes to coordinate statistical-power-heavy A/B runs with CI/CD schedules and oncall choreography so experiments don't step on releases or SRE maintenance windows. This is intentionally pragmatic — fast checklists, decision heuristics, and reminders for cross-functional handoffs.

Why this exists
- We regularly see noisy A/B results when CI jobs (integration tests, load tests) or infra maintenance overlap with experiment windows.
- Some A/Bs require long collection windows to hit power; those windows often collide with weekly deploy weekends and autoscaler tuning.
- Oncall needs a short, unambiguous playbook for experiment-related incidents (cost spikes, latency drift, behavioral regressions).

Scope and non-goals
- Scope: web-facing feature experiments, reranker/LLM model swaps, latency-sensitive canaries.
- Non-goals: full statistical primer (see Confluence note), deep causal-analysis recipes. This doc focuses on operational scheduling + incident choreography.

Key heuristics for scheduling experiments and CI
1) Experiment runway > CI cadence: If estimated collection time > 72 hours, schedule a maintenance-free window that avoids major CI runs (nightly load tests, regular DB migrations).
2) Tagging CI runs: Add "experiment-sensitive" tag to any CI job that is likely to affect production latency or DB state (e.g., synthetic load, end-to-end payment flows). Use this tag in scheduling calendar checks.
3) Backfill windows: Prefer staggered starts (start cohort A at 00:00 UTC, B at 04:00 UTC) only if the experiment and metric computation are tolerant of temporal offsets; avoid stagger for churn-prone metrics (retention).
4) Avoid heavy infra changes during active experiments: major infra PRs (kernel upgrades, autoscaler policy changes) should not target prod clusters used by experiments until observation window closes.

Power calculations + CI interplay (practical checklist)
- Before lock-in: quick power sketch (effect size, baseline rate, alpha=0.05, desired beta=0.8) and a rough sample-per-arm estimate. If per-arm > 50k, mark as "high-power" and route to scheduling guardrails.
- If high-power: create an event in the releases calendar with block reason=ExperimentHighPower and include CI blackout times. Notify SRE and Release Manager.
- Record expected token-cost and peak QPS in the experiment ticket; if projected QPS > 20% of cluster baseline, require capacity signoff.

CI schedule coordination patterns
- Light experiments (sample < 5k per arm): can run immediately with usual release blackout awareness. No extra CI coordination needed.
- Medium experiments (5k–50k per arm): check weekly CI calendar for heavy jobs; choose a start that avoids overlapping heavy jobs by +/- 12 hours.
- High experiments (>50k per arm): require explicit CI blackout of 24–72 hours for noise-sensitive metrics OR move to staged slice-based exposure to reduce noise.

Oncall choreography for experiments (roles and responsibilities)
- Experiment Owner (EO): product/pm owning hypothesis and basic metrics. Responsible for: experiment ticket, quick response, primary communicator.
- Experiment Steward (ES): engineer responsible for routing, feature-flag toggles, and rollout controls. Handles rapid rollback toggles and telemetry checks.
- SRE/Platform Liaison: validates capacity/signoff, executes infra rollbacks (if needed), and runs mitigation (scale-up/down).
- Incident Lead (oncall): default paged on metric thresholds; coordinates postmortem if incident escalates.
- Communications Coordinator: posts status updates to #release-orchestration and updates the experiment ticket and ops-runbook.

Incident triggers (examples + rapid actions)
- Latency SLO breach: 95p latency > SLO + 25% sustained for > 5 mins. Action: ES flip canary to fallback model OR route traffic to baseline, paged SRE.
- Token-cost spike: per-request token usage > expected + 50% for > 30 mins. Action: throttle traffic for experiment cohort; EO to pause experiment; cost owner notified.
- Behavioral drift (safety metrics): increase in safety flag rate or false-positive rate > threshold. Action: immediate human-reviewed sample collection, partial rollback to baseline, convene safety triage.
- Error-rate spike: 5xx rate > baseline * 3 for > 10 mins. Action: route traffic away from experiment, require SRE investigation.

Communication templates (short, copyable)
- Slack pager (initial): "[EXPERIMENT ALERT] <experiment-id> observed <metric> breach: <numeric>. EO=<owner>. Action taken: <rollback|throttle|ignore>. Paging SRE oncall. Ticket: <JIRA>."
- Post-rollback update: "Experiment <id> rolled back at <time> by <actor>. Summary: <brief>. Next steps: <investigate|re-run with new sample|close>"

Rollout and rollback knobs (practical quick list)
- Feature-flag toggle (instant rollback): always have one boolean toggle that returns 100% to baseline.
- Weight-based ramp: prefer 0->1%->5%->25%->100% with guardrail checks at each step for high-risk experiments. For high-power tests, add a 24-hour hold at 25%.
- Model-variant fallback: route to cheaper/shorter model variant if latency or token-cost drift observed.
- Emergency kill: standardized script (ops/kill-experiment.sh) that reversible disables experiment flag and flushes routing caches. Owner must link to the script in ticket.

Telemetry and signals (what to watch, why)
- User-facing signals: 95p/99p latency, error rates (5xx), time-to-first-token for streaming APIs, user abandonment rates.
- Cost signals: tokens/response, total tokens/hour, per-request CPU/GPU utilization.
- Quality signals: rerank precision hits, downstream CTR, safety flag counts.
- Statistical signals: running p-values are noisy — prefer pre-registered stopping rules. If using sequential tests, predefine alpha spending (O'Brien-Fleming or Pocock).

Experiment naming, tagging, and ticketing conventions (fast rules)
- Experiment ID: PROJ-shortname-YYYYMMDD-XX (XX = iteration). Example: HOSTED-chattimeout-20260214-01.
- Ticket tags: experiment, high-power, ci-blackout-required (optional), capacity-signoff. Use tags to seed calendar alerts.

Sample timeline for a high-power A/B (example)
- D-14: Draft hypothesis, rough power calc. EO files ticket with initial metrics and projected sample size.
- D-10: Capacity signoff and CI blackout request submitted; SRE acknowledges.
- D-7: Synthetic smoke tests and canary script verified; staging run passes.
- D-3: Calendar blackout confirmed (24–72h), oncall rotation notified.
- Day 0: Start experiment at 00:00 UTC. EO posts kickoff in #release-orchestration. ES monitors first 2 hours closely (latency/cost).
- Day 1–3: Hold at 25% for 24h, then advance to 100% if stable and still collecting power.
- End of window: stop collection, freeze metrics snapshot, run analysis in safe notebook, and publish results.

Open questions / decisions to make
- Do we want an automated calendar check that prevents scheduling of high-power experiments overlapping certain CI tags? (If yes, who owns the automation?)
- Which team owns the canonical experiment-cost-accounting dashboard? Product or Finance? Need a quick owner.
- How to enforce pre-registered stopping rules across teams without slowing down lightweight experiments?

Quick checklist before starting an experiment (tick list)
- [ ] Power calc in ticket
- [ ] Capacity signoff if QPS impact > 20%
- [ ] CI blackout requested for high-power
- [ ] Rollback toggle implemented and tested
- [ ] Oncall rota updated and SRE notified
- [ ] Safety metrics instrumented and alert thresholds set
- [ ] Communication plan + slack templates ready

Appendix: rapid runbook snippets
- Kill command: ops/kill-experiment.sh <experiment-id> (ES should have exec rights)
- Quick telemetry dashboard: /dashboards/experiment-overview?exp=<experiment-id>
- Smoke script: scripts/smoke-experiment.sh - runs 50 synthetic requests against new variant and compares latency to baseline.

Notes to self (working):
- @SRE: sketch automation for calendar-blocking and tag-based approval flow.
- @DevEx: can we add a lightweight web hook in PR merge flow that warns "active experiment in window" if PR touches routing logic?

References and examples
- Historical incident: HOSTED-20250112 (latency bump during nightly load test) — learnings: always check nightly load test schedule.
- Template tickets: see JIRA-AB-TEMPLATE in linked_artifacts.

If this doc is useful, next steps: turn the checklist into a simple UI in the Console's rollout flow (preflight checks) and prototype an automated calendar check that prevents high-power starts during heavy CI jobs.

End of scratchpad.
